EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Prior evidence points to depreciation conservatism as the most promising accrual channel, but a pure book-to-market interaction may still carry value-factor exposure. Blending book and earnings value tests whether conservative expense recognition supports a broader cheapness profile rather than only cheap balance-sheet stocks.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

HYPOTHESIS: High book-to-market firms should outperform when their depreciation policy is conservative relative to both their own history and industry peers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Depreciation norms differ materially across industries, so firm-relative depreciation surprises may partly reflect sector accounting structure. Industry-adjusting the depreciation-conservatism leg keeps the value interaction focused on unusually conservative accounting within comparable operating models.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Blended Value Underdepreciation Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(MUL(at, SUB(MA(RATIO(dp, at), 3), RATIO(dp, at))), ADD(ABS(ib), ABS(oancf))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that look cheap on book and earnings should underperform when current depreciation is unusually low relative to their recent policy.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This targets the short-side complement of depreciation-backed value: apparent cheapness can be inflated when accrual expense recognition falls below normal. Scaling the depreciation shortfall by earnings and cash-flow magnitude focuses on cases where the underdepreciation is economically meaningful rather than simply capital-intensive.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Depreciation Addback Cash Yield Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(dpc, ADD(ABS(oancf), ABS(ib))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that look cheap on operating cash flow should underperform when that cash flow depends heavily on depreciation and amortization addbacks.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Operating cash flow can look attractive because depreciation is added back, but high depreciation addbacks may proxy for capital consumption that cash-flow yield ignores. The signal is high when cheap cash flow is especially dependent on noncash accrual addbacks, creating a cash-flow value-trap test distinct from working-capital accruals.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Tax Accrual Conservatism Earnings Value
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), RATIO(txach, ADD(ABS(ib), ABS(oancf))))
HYPOTHESIS: High earnings-yield firms should outperform when tax accruals indicate reported earnings are conservative relative to cash taxes paid.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Positive tax accruals mean tax expense has reduced reported income more than current cash tax payment, so the mechanism supports earnings quality rather than undermining it. This corrected sign logic tests whether cheap reported earnings are especially attractive when they already bear conservative tax accrual charges.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Accelerating Working Capital Sales Trap
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(sale, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), ACCEL(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), DELTA(txp, 1))), sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that look cheap on sales should underperform when noncash operating working-capital accruals are accelerating relative to sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: A high sales yield may be a trap if each dollar of reported sales increasingly requires receivables, inventory, or other operating working capital. The acceleration term focuses on deteriorating sales quality rather than the static working-capital accrual level that has produced mixed portfolio evidence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Conservative Depreciation Value Blend---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the archived "Depreciation Conservatism Book Interaction" with RANK(B/M) swapped for SUMRANK(B/M, E/P), a cosmetic re-weighting of the value leg whose stated motivation (reducing value-factor exposure) is backwards since adding earnings yield increases, not reduces, HML loading.

---CRITIQUE Industry Relative Depreciation Conservatism Book---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible, mechanism-driven refinement of the archive's strongest result — industry-adjusting the own-history depreciation surprise removes sector-common accounting/asset-mix variation and is a genuinely different conditioning construct rather than a rescaling, though it remains a close relative of that prior signal.

---CRITIQUE Blended Value Underdepreciation Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Near-duplicate of the archived "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap" (same scaled depreciation-shortfall conditioner, same sign, same construction) with only the value leg widened to SUMRANK, so it adds little new information beyond the already-evaluated short side.

---CRITIQUE Depreciation Addback Cash Yield Trap---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A coherent and previously untested conditioner (D&A addback dependence of OCF as unpriced capital consumption) that complements rather than duplicates the archive's working-capital and maintenance-depreciation work, though dpc/(|oancf|+|ib|) is largely a capital-intensity/industry proxy so any result will need an industry-neutral robustness check.

---CRITIQUE Tax Accrual Conservatism Earnings Value---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The sign logic is internally consistent and the txach interpretation is correct, but this is substantially a sign-flipped repackaging of the archived "Tax Deferred Cash Yield Trap" (same conditioner, same scaler, adjacent value leg) whose positive fmb slope came with negligible alpha and ~6% coverage, so the "new" evidence is likely the same underlying result relabeled.

---CRITIQUE Accelerating Working Capital Sales Trap---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The acceleration framing is a legitimately distinct construct from the archive's level and one-period-change accrual conditioners, but taking a second difference of a ratio whose numerator is already an annual first difference stacks three layers of annual noise and will require several extra years of history, so expect weak power and degraded coverage.
